profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company, traded as CRNC and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts. Its site describes it as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, built on CaLLM, its family of language models, which the company says enables natural, multimodal and safe interactions. It also describes work with Microsoft on Zero Trust architecture and layered AI security for in-car assistants, and lists Kaivan Karimi as Business Development Senior Director and Frank Kaleck as Director Industry Advisory Automotive at Microsoft.

Among the products the site highlights is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection (EVD), which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles and can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, with a demonstration by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich, and says the company is moving to advance generative AI and LLM-powered innovation for automotive and transportation.

The company reported third quarter results with revenue up 12% year over year, connected services revenue up 20% year over year, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. Its litigation exposure is recorded in Massachusetts, with 97 matters.
